articles.title: Beyond the Green Squares: Turning GitHub Activity Into Things Worth Keeping
articles.excerpt: A series of small, playful projects built from your GitHub activity. Try them on your own profile, keep the results, and help decide what I build next. You push code for a whole year. Late nights, tin…
articles.body: A series of small, playful projects built from your GitHub activity. Try them on your own profile, keep the results, and help decide what I build next. You push code for a whole year. Late nights, tiny fixes, big launches, reviews for other people's work. And GitHub shows all of that as a grid of green squares. Squares are fine. But I keep wondering what that year would look like if it became something you could hold, share, or stick on a wall. So I'm starting Beyond the Green Squares . What this series is Each post is one small project that turns GitHub activity into something unexpected. The rules are simple: You can try it yourself. Every project works with a public GitHub username, no sign-in needed. You can keep the result. Download it, share it, or print it. The numbers stay honest.

articles.title: A tiny daily side quest that sends you outside.
articles.excerpt: What I Built I'm a developer, and most of my day looks like this: laptop at work, phone on the way home, laptop again at night. I know I should go outside more. The problem is never time. The problem…
articles.body: What I Built I'm a developer, and most of my day looks like this: laptop at work, phone on the way home, laptop again at night. I know I should go outside more. The problem is never time. The problem is that "go outside" is too vague, so I never do it. So I built Grass Quest : a small web app that gives you one short outdoor mission every day , written for today's real weather in your city. Here's how it works: You tell it your city once. It checks the real weather: temperature, rain chance, wind and sunset time. An open-weight AI model writes a 15 to 45 minute mission that fits that weather. On a rainy day, you get a short, safe walk, not a hike. You put the phone away and go outside. You come back with 1 to 3 photos.

articles.title: Make Fragment Epoch an Invariant Before a Restarted Scorer Publishes a Grade
articles.excerpt: I still replay a grading-lane fixture I built for this review, because a green dashboard can hide a lying grade. A worker wrote fragment one, the eval server restarted, and a new worker wrote another…
articles.body: I still replay a grading-lane fixture I built for this review, because a green dashboard can hide a lying grade. A worker wrote fragment one, the eval server restarted, and a new worker wrote another fragment one. The delayed fragment two from the first epoch then arrived, and the publisher appended it anyway. Would you trust that mixed score inside a canary gate, or would you halt the lane? The common implementation treats each partial score as an append-only log keyed only by attempt id. That key alone is not enough, because a restart creates a new generation that still shares the attempt. The invariant I want is narrower than idempotent writes: a grade may contain fragments from only one epoch.

Life sciences data management now wins or loses on lineage, quality, access control, and reproducibility. Its drug-development guidance centers model credibility on a defined context of use, and FDA says CDER drew on experience with more than 500 submissions containing AI components from 2016–2023.

articles.title: How AI Helps Detect Camera Tampering, Masking, and Malfunction
articles.excerpt: Most security teams find out about a blocked camera the same way. Something goes missing, someone pulls the footage, and the recording shows an hour of black screen, a greasy blur, or a crisp view of…
articles.body: Most security teams find out about a blocked camera the same way. Something goes missing, someone pulls the footage, and the recording shows an hour of black screen, a greasy blur, or a crisp view of a wall. That blind spot is the first problem good AI security cameras solve. Before AI CCTV cameras can flag an intruder or a fire, they have to confirm the camera can still see. I'd argue this is the most underrated job in AI security surveillance , because every other alert depends on it. This post breaks down how tampering, masking, and malfunction detection works under the hood, where it gets fooled, and what to ask before you trust a vendor's demo.

articles.body: As artificial intelligence becomes an everyday essential, privacy has emerged as its greatest compromise. Mainstream platforms like ChatGPT and Google Gemini rely heavily on persistent user profiles, behavioral tracking, and vast datasets — often drawn directly from your prompts — to train their models. Enter DuckDuckGo AI Chat (accessible via Duck.ai ). Promoted as a privacy-first alternative, it promises access to leading AI models without corporate surveillance. It’s a tempting offer for sure. But is DuckDuckGo AI genuinely a better alternative to Gemini and ChatGPT , or does its focus on anonymity come at the cost of capability?

articles.body: Friday, October 16, 2026 Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. articles.body: Credit: NASA Editor’s note: This release was updated Oct. 8, 2026 with the formal name of the summit. NASA is launching two new science and technology initiatives to deepen scientific understanding and accelerate the innovation that will shape America’s future in space. The initiatives are announced in conjunction with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s (OSTP) “Science: A Golden Age Summit” in Washington on Thursday with top U.S. agency leaders. The programs reflect NASA’s commitment to pioneering research and transformative technologies and advancing the Trump Administration’s vision as outlined in the July report to the President, Science: A New Golden Age. One focuses on peer review and the other on fellowship researchers.
